And you're there"}, {'start': '29.440', 'end': '33.520', 'text': 'in the middle of it all wondering: What the hell is going on?'}, {'start': '33.520', 'end': '38.840', 'text': "It's not a science fiction scene.  It's not the beginning of The Walking Dead, nor is it a dystopia ripped"}, {'start': '38.840', 'end': '44.720', 'text': "from Mark Ellsberg's Blackout.  This is what happened and we saw it with our own eyes.  On"}, {'start': '44.720', 'end': '50.880', 'text': 'Monday, April 28, 2025, Spain and Portugal experienced the largest power outage in their'}, {'start': '50.880', 'end': '55.640', 'text': 'history.  The power outage also left Andorra and part of southern'}, {'start': '55.640', 'end': '61.160', 'text': 'France without electricity, compounding the impact of the blackout.  A massive blackout that lasted'}, {'start': '61.160', 'end': '64.920', 'text': 'for hours paralyzed cities, infrastructure, and'}, {'start': '64.920', 'end': '70.120', 'text': 'communications... and made us look back to a time when we still lived without electricity.  You'}, {'start': '70.120', 'end': '75.920', 'text': 'might wonder: How can a modern country, full of satellites, servers,'}, {'start': '75.920', 'end': '82.800', 'text': 'switchboards, and sensors, in the 21st century, fall into total darkness from one second to the next?'}, {'start': '82.800', 'end': '87.800', 'text': "Well, today, we're going to shine a light—literally and figuratively—on this"}, {'start': '87.800', 'end': '93.880', 'text': "everyday yet mysterious phenomenon: electricity.  We'll discover what really happened during the"}, {'start': '93.880', 'end': '101.040', 'text': 'Great Blackout, and above all, why our world depends so much on something as invisible as it is fragile.'}, {'start': '101.040', 'end': '104.960', 'text': 'Are you ready?  I am GG Prigo, this is the science of sciences,'}, {'start': '104.960', 'end': '110.760', 'text': 'here we always see that the known is limited and the unknown is infinite.  Want to know more?'}, {'start': '110.760', 'end': '117.400', 'text': "Well... let's explore!  Introduction"}, {'start': '123.440', 'end': '128.120', 'text': 'Yes, what comes out of our light bulbs is not a modern luxury.  It is the beating heart of'}, {'start': '128.120', 'end': '131.760', 'text': 'our civilization.  To begin to understand this,'}, {'start': '131.760', 'end': '138.760', 'text': 'we need to look at what exactly happened.  At 12:32 p.m., an unusual event rocked the'}, {'start': '138.760', 'end': '144.720', 'text': 'Iberian electricity grid:'}, {'start': '144.720', 'end': '151.240', 'text': "15 gigawatts of power suddenly disappeared—more than half of the country's total consumption at the time.  Yes, suddenly.  As if someone had uprooted a"}, {'start': '151.240', 'end': '155.120', 'text': 'fundamental part of the system.  To give you an idea, this is'}, {'start': '155.120', 'end': '161.640', 'text': 'roughly equivalent to cutting off twice'}, {'start': '161.640', 'end': '167.040', 'text': "Spain's operational nuclear capacity immediately.  Real anger.  It was like being in the middle of a game of Jenga and someone was"}, {'start': '167.040', 'end': '171.480', 'text': 'pulling out the tile that was keeping the entire tower upright.  The'}, {'start': '171.480', 'end': '177.640', 'text': 'system has crashed, the grid has been disconnected from Europe, and we have gone into power survival mode.'}, {'start': '177.640', 'end': '179.920', 'text': 'This is where things get more interesting.'}, {'start': '179.920', 'end': '185.280', 'text': "Because we're so used to flipping a switch and seeing the light come on... that we"}, {'start': '185.280', 'end': '189.520', 'text': 'forget to ask the key question: What is electricity, really?'}, {'start': '189.520', 'end': '195.160', 'text': 'No, they are not magic lines.  Electricity is the orderly movement of electrons.'}, {'start': '195.160', 'end': '200.400', 'text': 'Millions and millions of them, flowing through cables, like an invisible river of'}, {'start': '200.400', 'end': '206.120', 'text': 'tiny particles that give life to our cities, our homes, our hospitals, our satellites... and to you.'}, {'start': '206.120', 'end': '209.080', 'text': 'Imagine it this way: if water flows in a river,'}, {'start': '209.080', 'end': '213.160', 'text': 'electrons flow in wires.  It is not that there is a “thing” that travels'}, {'start': '213.160', 'end': '218.600', 'text': "as if it were a train.  no!  It's the electrons of the atoms themselves that are moving collectively, a"}, {'start': '218.600', 'end': '222.880', 'text': 'kind of microscopic collapse.  Here comes the really amazing thing:'}, {'start': '222.880', 'end': '228.080', 'text': 'electricity is not stored on a large scale.  They are generated in real time.'}, {'start': '228.080', 'end': '232.080', 'text': 'Every time you turn on a light bulb, there is a power station generating'}, {'start': '232.080', 'end': '236.800', 'text': "that energy at that specific moment.  It's as if every time you turn on the tap,"}, {'start': '236.800', 'end': '240.400', 'text': "there's a worker on the other end, pumping water just for you."}, {'start': '240.400', 'end': '246.120', 'text': 'Can you imagine what that means on a national level?  Every millisecond, the electrical grid must balance the'}, {'start': '246.120', 'end': '252.000', 'text': 'energy we generate with the energy we consume.  No more, no less.  A little more... and the system is'}, {'start': '252.000', 'end': '257.560', 'text': "overloaded.  A little less...and explode.  And that's exactly what happened: the"}, {'start': '257.560', 'end': '262.680', 'text': 'massive loss of generation triggered severe grid volatility.'}, {'start': '262.680', 'end': '266.680', 'text': 'It was as if the violin player had stopped plucking the strings and the music had turned'}, {'start': '266.680', 'end': '271.320', 'text': 'into a hellish scream.  Spain and Portugal, within'}, {'start': '271.320', 'end': '276.760', 'text': 'seconds, were plunged into darkness.  In the cities, the chaos was immediate:'}, {'start': '276.760', 'end': '281.560', 'text': 'supermarkets had endless lines of people buying water and candles.  Traffic lights'}, {'start': '281.560', 'end': '288.400', 'text': 'deaths create massive traffic jams.  Battery-powered portable radios are selling like hot cakes.'}, {'start': '288.400', 'end': '293.440', 'text': 'All this, in just a few minutes.  Did you know that in major power outages in'}, {'start': '293.440', 'end': '299.800', 'text': "New York, the first thing to go out are the batteries?  Well, today, in Spain, we've revived that."}, {'start': '299.800', 'end': '304.800', 'text': 'In the midst of the digital age, the battery-powered radio—yes, that technological artifact—has once again become'}, {'start': '304.800', 'end': '310.840', 'text': 'our only means of communication with the outside world.  This leads us to a much deeper question:'}, {'start': '310.840', 'end': '315.160', 'text': 'What does our society really support?  Electricity...or'}, {'start': '315.160', 'end': '320.840', 'text': "something more basic we've forgotten?  To understand what went wrong today, we first need to"}, {'start': '320.840', 'end': '326.440', 'text': 'understand what exactly an electrical grid is.  Imagine all the electricity in a country'}, {'start': '326.440', 'end': '331.480', 'text': 'as one giant symphony orchestra.  Every tool—nuclear plants,'}, {'start': '331.480', 'end': '338.040', 'text': 'hydropower plants, wind farms, solar panels—plays its part.  But for the music to sound good,'}, {'start': '338.040', 'end': '344.400', 'text': 'everyone has to be perfectly in sync. transcript: [{'start': '0.200', 'end': '5.440', 'text': "In a world where everything is designed to be consumed and replaced, where creativity seems to have been relegated to the background, have you ever wondered if there is another way? We 've been told that originality is for a select few, but today we're going to challenge that idea. We live in the era of the prefabricated and the instant. And, let's be honest, it's exhausting sometimes. We feel like we're missing something, right? That spark, that connection with what we create with our own hands. But what if I told you there was a way back? A path where the survival of your creativity depends on your ingenuity... and your hands. Get ready to enter a different game, a game where the prize is the satisfaction of saying: 'I did it!' Inspired by a phenomenon that tested the limits of survival and strategy, we are going to recreate some of its iconic elements. But not to compete for life or death, but to relive the pleasure of building and demonstrating that creativity is never lost. So, get ready for the Creative Survival DIY roundup. We start with the strength and precision of the stone: Stone Throw, a game that forces you to measure your strength and trust your creation. We will create our own 'stones' to practice this ancient art... with a modern twist. We start with the big stone. And now, the secret of weight: rice, lentils or even small metal balls. We seal with another piece of gray cardboard. For the characteristic curve, we moisten two rectangles of gray cardboard. We wrap our 'stone' and an arch-shaped piece with plastic. We cover with moistened cardboard. We can secure it with tape or rubber bands and let it dry overnight. If you want extra solidity, you can put hot silicone on the edges, smoothing it with a little baking paper. Look how beautiful these rings and this bracelet are. They are from Perimade and I love them because they give a special and delicate touch to any look, even a casual one. So, if you like them as much as I do, I will leave you the link to their products in the video description. Now, the actual stone texture. We will mix school glue or carpenter's glue with pieces of toilet paper to create that paste. Once the dough is completely dry, we paint dark gray. With the dry brush and light gray acrylic paint, we will highlight the texture so that it looks like it has been outdoors for centuries... or at least, that it has character. For the small stone, we will use polystyrene. We will cut the shape with a cutter, refining the details. We hollow out the base and fill it with rice to give it weight with hot silicone and repeat the texture and painting steps. Now you have your stones ready for a throwing duel, and without crystals in the way, please! Let's start with Ddakji, a game that tests your aim and the resistance of your creations. We will need two sheets of Din A4 paper. It can be any color you want; In this case, we are going to make it blue. We fold each sheet in half and, to ensure that it has that resistance, we laminate both sheets. We fold each rectangle into three equal parts and then fold the corners to form triangles. If you want extra security, a piece of double-sided tape on the corners can be your best friend. We put the pieces in a cross shape and fold the triangles inward. Now you have your Ddakjis ready for friendly combat! From the art of folding and throwing we move to the dance of balance. So, the next challenge invites us to dominate the rotation: The Trompo, a classic toy that in this universe takes on a special meaning. We will cut seven circles of gray EVA foam and roll them to form cones, making sure the angle is the same in all of them. We stack the cones to shape our top. And if all this seemed too complicated to you, don't worry because I'm going to leave you the template with all the pieces in the video description. A pencil will be our central axis and, once again, rice comes into play to give it weight and stability. To paint the details of this iconic star, I am going to use Ohuhu brand colored pencils. Remember that I am going to leave you all the materials that I am going to use in the description of the video. We painted the top silver. We'll glue on the star design carefully and there you have it: your very own top, ready to defy gravity and prove that creativity never stops spinning. Taking advantage of this wave of creativity inspired by the game, I bring you an express idea that combines the nostalgia of the first season with a quick DIY project: Keychains of the mythical Dalgona cookie! It is perfect for creating complementary keychains with different designs. So you can give them to your friends or family. Once you have released the design of the cookie, paint to give it that recognizable color on both sides! My allies were these acrylic markers from the Ohuhu brand. They cover wonderfully and are super easy to use, and they also come with two different tips. You will find all the materials that I am using in the video description. To cut the round shape and engrave the interior design in wood, I relied on the precision of my laser machine. But if you don't have a laser, no problem. Use gray cardboard (a good challenge for your cutter) or foam board for something thicker and simpler. So, you now have your original keychain made without the risk of breaking. Our next challenge is the Gong-gi. It is a traditional game that may seem simple, but hides an art of skill and patience. The base will be a cardboard. We cut a strip, peel a layer to expose those characteristic waves. We will form a ring and glue it. If you want a cool shortcut, mix wood glue with acrylic paint. We add a cardboard circle inside and fill with hot silicone. If you don't have hot glue, you can also use rice. This will give it the necessary weight and consistency. We cut the iconic symbols from thin cardboard and glued them to each side of the pieces. But where will we keep the precious pieces? In a wooden style box of course! We cut a long strip of gray cardboard. We moisten it with a little water to make it more malleable and give it the desired shape. We let it dry overnight. We painted everything with a brown acrylic paint base. Once dry, comes the magic of the wood texture. With a dry brush, we applied different shades of brown, dragging the paint gently to imitate the grain. You can make some fine lines with a brown marker to complete the illusion. And voila! A box that looks like it was carved by an expert, but made by you. From the game of skill we move on to the expressionless vigilante: Jeji, the vacant-looking vigilante who has become a symbol of the second season. We start with a humble base, a simple plastic lid that we will transform. Now, the iconic waves. A 13-pointed star will be our ally so that each wave has its vital space. We cut the wooden sticks to 1.5 cm. We will glue them following our stellar guide. And if a stick refuses to stick, don't despair. Sometimes even the most stoic sentinels need an extra boost of glue... or motivation! Then, we wrap it with a strip of EVA rubber. We cover the base with a clean finish. A bath of yellow acrylic paint gives it its characteristic vibrant tone. For the fringes, those disturbing 'legs', we will use metallic curtains. We group them, tie them and cut them to size. We pass them through the central hole in the base. If they get tangled, take a deep breath. Think you're unraveling the mysteries of the universe... or at least, those of Jeji. To give it weight and stability, a little rice on the base. We seal with glue and EVA foam. And if you use too much glue, it's okay; Jeji will just have a little more clingy 'personality'. Finally, his enigmatic face. We will draw the design on blue paper with a white acrylic marker. In this case, I am going to use this one from the Ohuhu brand. We laminate to protect it and glue it. transcript: [{'start': '0.160', 'end': '4.720', 'text': "One Piece is an incredible work, but I'm not going to lie: it's difficult to start watching. With"}, {'start': '4.720', 'end': '9.360', 'text': 'more than a thousand episodes, the idea of \u200b\u200bdiving into this universe can scare anyone. My Experience with One Piece.'}, {'start': '25.160', 'end': '30.400', 'text': "I've never been a big fan of piracy stories and, honestly, I've always been too lazy to download"}, {'start': '30.400', 'end': '35.480', 'text': "One Piece to watch. But after it came on Netflix, I decided to give it a chance. And that's"}, {'start': '35.480', 'end': '41.200', 'text': 'when I realized: people were right. Eiichiro Oda truly is a genius. The construction of the world,'}, {'start': '41.200', 'end': '45.960', 'text': 'the characters, the emotions... all of this made me fall in love with the work.'}, {'start': '45.960', 'end': '49.320', 'text': 'Iconic Moments. One Piece has some scenes'}, {'start': '49.320', 'end': '56.320', 'text': 'that make it worth watching 500, 600 episodes just to feel the emotion for the first time. This made me become a fan of him and One Piece.'}, {'start': '199.000', 'end': '205.200', 'text': "But without a doubt, the most iconic scene of all is when Luffy punches a Tenryuubito. And if you don't"}, {'start': '205.200', 'end': '210.200', 'text': 'know what a Tenryuubito is, they are members of the "world nobility", an arrogant elite who'}, {'start': '210.200', 'end': '215.520', 'text': 'live above everyone else, treating ordinary people like trash. They dress ridiculously,'}, {'start': '215.520', 'end': '220.520', 'text': "with bubble helmets so they don't breathe the same air as normal people. This is"}, {'start': '220.520', 'end': '224.880', 'text': 'very reminiscent of our politicians: distant from reality, living in bubbles of'}, {'start': '224.880', 'end': '230.000', 'text': 'privilege and believing that they are above the laws. When Luffy lands that punch,'}, {'start': '230.000', 'end': '236.760', 'text': "it's like the cry of millions of people who suffer from injustice every day."}, {'start': '508.840', 'end': '511.960', 'text': "It's one of the most satisfying moments in the entire work."}, {'start': '511.960', 'end': '517.760', 'text': "It's a good thing that One Piece is a long work, because to understand these deep messages, you"}, {'start': '517.760', 'end': '523.720', 'text': 'need to watch many episodes and get involved with the world created by Oda. If it were a short and direct series'}, {'start': '523.720', 'end': '530.280', 'text': ', with such open criticism, there would certainly be countries where the government would try to'}, {'start': '530.280', 'end': '536.160', 'text': 'ban it from being shown. But as everything is diluted over a thousand episodes, it ends up going'}, {'start': '536.160', 'end': '543.080', 'text': "unnoticed by those who aren't paying attention. [{'start': '0.240', 'end': '3.520', 'text': 'We are the generation that talks the most about

.  She clicked on old posts,'}, {'start': '523.840', 'end': '530.760', 'text': 'looked at photos, and browsed comments.

But something began to change inside her.'}, {'start': '586.960', 'end': '593.520', 'text': 'Something that was neither anger nor disappointment,

Perhaps not everything is as it seems.'}, {'start': '600.600', 'end': '607.160', 'text': "Heidemarie didn't know it yet, but in
that moment she had opened the first door - a door"}, {'start': '607.160', 'end': '612.040', 'text': 'behind which there was no love waiting, but
a truth that weighed more heavily than any'}, {'start': '612.040', 'end': '617.400', 'text': 'promise.  Despite the quiet doubts in her

She didn't want to become suspicious, didn't want to"}, {'start': '622.440', 'end': '629.000', 'text': 'lose the little routine that gave her security.

Between conversations about the latest'}, {'start': '646.360', 'end': '651.760', 'text': 'local gossip and the upcoming spring market,
Hannelore casually mentioned an article in'}, {'start': '651.760', 'end': '658.120', 'text': 'the newspaper: a pensioner from the region had been cheated out of

politely, but internally she dismissed the thought'}, {'start': '672.320', 'end': '679.080', 'text': '.  Such stories happened to others,
not to her.  Muhammed was no longer a stranger,'}, {'start': '679.080', 'end': '684.240', 'text': 'no longer an anonymous chat contact.  He had
long since become a part of her everyday life,'}, {'start': '684.240', 'end': '690.480', 'text': 'with his loving messages, the little
stories about his daughter, the quiet,'}, {'start': '690.480', 'end': '696.080', 'text': 'honest way he spoke about his life.  That
same week, a late-night'}, {'start': '696.080', 'end': '701.920', 'text': 'television documentary was on, and she happened to

.  Women spoke of men'}, {'start': '708.640', 'end': '713.920', 'text': 'they had met abroad,
of big promises, marriage plans,'}, {'start': '713.920', 'end': '721.080', 'text': 'and in the end of the loss of money, trust, and

affected, heard their stories – and'}, {'start': '731.800', 'end': '738.560', 'text': 'yet felt nothing that she related to herself
.  Muhammad was not like these men.'}, {'start': '738.560', 'end': '745.520', 'text': 'He had never asked her for money, never pressured her,

Instead, she turned off the television,"}, {'start': '782.200', 'end': '788.320', 'text': 'went to sleep, and brushed aside the underlying

But although she kept"}, {'start': '792.720', 'end': '799.080', 'text': 'calming herself down, Heidemarie felt

a thought would come to her so quickly that she'}, {'start': '811.640', 'end': '818.880', 'text': "could hardly grasp it: What if I'm wrong?
She pushed it aside, tried to"}, {'start': '818.880', 'end': '824.240', 'text': 'drown it out – with logic, with hope, with the

, she wasn't a special find,"}, {'start': '930.720', 'end': '936.840', 'text': 'she was part of a list.  A list on which

And Muhammad was not the lost widower'}, {'start': '943.120', 'end': '950.000', 'text': 'seeking comfort – he was part of a system.
The thought of the many kind words,'}, {'start': '950.000', 'end': '954.880', 'text': 'the seemingly personal conversations,
the pictures and little stories they'}, {'start': '954.880', 'end': '961.640', 'text': 'had shared made her shudder.
None of it was meant just for her.'}, {'start': '961.640', 'end': '968.920', 'text': 'None of it was unique or genuine.  It was
a script, tested, adapted, refined,'}, {'start': '968.920', 'end': '973.720', 'text': 'perfectly tailored to people like her.
People who had perhaps lost too much'}, {'start': '973.720', 'end': '979.600', 'text': 'and remained silent for too long, until even a
stranger could light a familiar light.'}, {'start': '979.600', 'end': '985.560', 'text': 'Heidemarie closed the laptop as if she could
undo what she had seen.  But the'}, {'start': '985.560', 'end': '991.560', 'text': 'list wasn’t just on her screen –
it was burned into her consciousness.'}, {'start': '991.560', 'end': '996.880', 'text': 'For the first time, she felt that there was no safe

n't open apps,\xa0 avoided anything"}, {'start': '1016.720', 'end': '1022.680', 'text': "that might remind her of Muhammed.

: "I'm coming. I want you to see'}, {'start': '1064.760', 'end': '1069.880', 'text': 'that I'm real."  The promise that

The pressure that she had previously only'}, {'start': '1109.520', 'end': '1114.960', 'text': 'felt subconsciously suddenly became

, felt strange, as if she were'}, {'start': '1194.960', 'end': '1201.840', 'text': 'suddenly standing on thin ice.  Every step

On the morning of the expected day, she sat'}, {'start': '1207.320', 'end': '1213.040', 'text': 'numb on the sofa.  She had muted her cell phone

Spain, under changing identities.'}, {'start': '1307.600', 'end': '1312.800', 'text': 'The list that Heidemarie had found was

In the days following the conversation with the'}, {'start': '1362.640', 'end': '1369.200', 'text': "criminal police, Heidemarie remained silent.  She did
n't speak to her children, not to her friends,"}, {'start': '1369.200', 'end': '1374.080', 'text': 'not even to the neighbor who usually

In the weeks and months of their'}, {'start': '1482.000', 'end': '1486.160', 'text': "contact, it hadn't just remained the 80 euros
.  Again and again, Muhammed had"}, {'start': '1486.160', 'end': '1491.960', 'text': 'made small requests – for school fees, for

.  It was never large sums at once,'}, {'start': '1498.000', 'end': '1504.000', 'text': 'always in small steps.  But when Heidemarie

transcript: [{'start': '0.240', 'end': '4.880', 'text': 'The myth that humans only use 10% of their brain'}, {'start': '4.880', 'end': '8.840', 'text': 'has been widely spread through the public and media for a long time, but it is scientifically unfounded.'}, {'start': '8.840', 'end': '14.120', 'text': 'The origin of this myth comes from the 19th century American psychologist William James who noted that'}, {'start': '14.120', 'end': '18.600', 'text': 'humans use only a portion of their potential.'}, {'start': '18.600', 'end': '23.599', 'text': 'Afterwards, the expression “use only 10%” appeared in self-development books in the 1930s and'}, {'start': '23.599', 'end': '29.000', 'text': 'became established as a fact, and was often used in popular culture, including the movie Lucy.'}, {'start': '29.000', 'end': '33.920', 'text': 'However, modern neuroscience research shows that we use multiple areas of the brain simultaneously.'}, {'start': '33.920', 'end': '39.960', 'text': 'As a result of brain imaging such as MRI, it has been confirmed that several parts of the brain are activated through simple actions or thoughts.'}, {'start': '39.960', 'end': '42.760', 'text': 'In reality, if 90% of your brain is idle,'}, {'start': '42.760', 'end': '46.800', 'text': "there shouldn't be any problems when that area is damaged, but in reality,"}, {'start': '46.800', 'end': '51.680', 'text': 'even a small brain injury can cause significant disability. Experts'}, {'start': '51.680', 'end': '58.356', 'text': 'emphasize that the claim that only 10% of the brain is used has no scientific basis and that the brain is always active as a whole.'}]

As if, after so much stumbling, so much fighting, so much falling... you could no longer feel at peace again. What happens to the soul when it breaks? What do we do when we don\'t know how to repair it? Today I want to share a very deep meditation with you. It is not a traditional gospel parable, but it has enormous spiritual power. It is a mystical meditation, attributed to Jesus, collected in the work The God-Man, by María Valtorta. Before continuing, I am going to invite you to subscribe so our videos have greater reach and more people can enjoy them. It does not appear as such in the New Testament, but it is strongly inspired by the real words of Jesus that are in the Gospels, especially in that teaching where he tells us that no one puts a new patch on an old garment, because the new is ruined and the old does not resist. Today we are going to immerse ourselves in this reflection and see what it means when Jesus compares the soul to a cloth that can tear and above all what we can do when we no longer know how to fix it. We take the texts from Man-God, a series of mystical writings by María Valtorta, a 20th century Italian laywoman, who claims to have received visions of the life of Jesus. This reflection is a path to think, feel and let God touch our hearts through a powerful image like the fabric of the soul. Jesus says in this meditation: “I compare the soul to a piece of cloth. When it is unfounded it is new, it has no breaks; only the original stain...¨ That is, when we come into the world, our soul arrives pure, complete, intact. Like a new garment, without seams, tears or stains. But over time, due to wrong decisions, due to wounds we receive and also due to the mistakes we make, that fabric, which is the soul, deteriorates. It gets dirty, it gets stained. It is weakened by vices. It is torn by reckless decisions. It is broken by emotional and spiritual wounds. And not only does it break, but sometimes we try to fix it badly. Like when someone puts any patch, without care, just to cover it up. And what happens is that the original fabric breaks even more. Now what do we do when we are broken? In this meditation Jesus tells us something very important: "Once broken, you should not make a poorly made patch, which would cause other tears... you must do patient and careful work to repair the damage." This tells us about the path of healing, and Jesus tells us: "Do not cover up, Do not mend badly, Do not deceive yourself. If your soul is wounded, do not hide it. Come to me, because I can restore your integrity." And what do we do with pride? Jesus also talks about spiritual pride and says: "The greater the damage in the soul, the more a man tries to hide it with poorly made solutions... and sometimes he does not even ask for help." He who is wounded by diseases, caused in him by unworthy vices, is ashamed of his wounds, and sometimes, he is so completely foolish that he keeps them hidden until the stench reveals them. But then it is too late to remedy it. In this case it refers to broken people, who do not open up to anyone. That they do not ask for forgiveness or that they do not open themselves to God. Jesus says: "The humble is brave. The proud is a coward." The humble one says: "Lord, I am wounded. Heal me." On the other hand, the proud prefers to die with the wound rather than show it. Jesus says: "There are many souls who, out of pride in not having to confess an initial guilt, fall into despair, because they are without God, and saying: "It is too late." And thus, many souls die inside, because they do not have the courage to say: "I am wrong, but I want to change." And Jesus speaks of the wounds and says: "The wounds that a soul has suffered will always be seen. But the soul undertakes its battle and, consequently, receives wounds. The wounds that a soul receives from fighting are not a reason for shame, but for honor. Let\'s think about the following: a person covered with scars, who fought, that fell, is not despised. On the contrary, she is honest. So, if you fought against your weaknesses, if you went through spiritual battles... your wounds don\'t make you less, they make you brave. The key is to go to the doctor of the soul, and say: "Lord, here I am. I fought. I fell. But I do not give up. Heal me. Prepare my soul for new battles." What does this meditation want to tell us? That Jesus does not reject us because we are broken. It does not require us to be perfect before approaching. The only thing he asks of us is that we not hide it, that we not deceive ourselves, that we have the humility to say: "I need help." Jesus says: "The mercy of God is stronger than any illness, greater than any error." So, if today we feel that our soul is like an old, torn, stained cloth... Let\'s not try to cover it. Let\'s not put a self-help patch on it. Let\'s not pretend that everything is fine. Jesus invites us to go see him, because he does not put patches or patches. He makes you new. I invite you to take a moment of silence, close your eyes and think: How is your soul today? Do you have any part of your soul broken? Do you dare to let God truly heal you? If this message touched your heart, share it with someone who might be struggling inside, needing to hear this meditation. I hope you liked this video. If you liked it, I\'m going to ask you to give it a like. This way it has more reach and distribution. We invite you to follow us on social networks, as well as subscribe to the channel, so you are aware of all the videos that we upload. My name is Nicolás and we\'ll see you in the next video.'}]

[{'start': '0.560', 'end': '6.160', 'text': 'Desperately climbing away from an all-consuming\xa0
ooze doesn’t sound like a jolly good time,'}, {'start': '6.160', 'end': '12.480', 'text': 'yet somehow, White Knuckle makes it ruthlessly\xa0
addictive. Thanks to extremely tight controls,'}, {'start': '12.480', 'end': '19.440', 'text': 'a slew of challenging-but-fair obstacle courses,\xa0
and a dystopian world so bizarre that I *need*'}, {'start': '19.440', 'end': '27.120', 'text': 'to know more about it, White Knuckle has\xa0
completely devoured my past few days.'}, {'start': '36.880', 'end': '42.800', 'text': 'At its core, White Knuckle is an astonishingly\xa0
simple game. You can jump, you can sprint,'}, {'start': '42.800', 'end': '47.920', 'text': "and you can grab onto things with either hand in\xa0
order to climb. If you're feeling particularly"}, {'start': '47.920', 'end': '53.760', 'text': 'spicy, you can even latch onto ledges with\xa0
both hands to hoist yourself up faster.'}, {'start': '53.760', 'end': '59.440', 'text': "What you can't do is hold on forever as your\xa0
titular white knuckles will quickly start turning"}, {'start': '59.440', 'end': '66.000', 'text': 'bright red, thus warning you that your stamina is\xa0
running out and that your grip is about to fail.'}, {'start': '66.000', 'end': '72.160', 'text': "To avoid a grizzly fall you'll need to either find\xa0
a perch to rest up on, or if safe haven is nowhere"}, {'start': '72.160', 'end': '78.720', 'text': 'to be found, alternate between each hand to buy\xa0
yourself just enough time to crawl to safety.'}, {'start': '78.720', 'end': '85.120', 'text': 'If you find yourself in a situation where progress\xa0
looks impossible - or if you spot a potential'}, {'start': '85.120', 'end': '92.880', 'text': 'shortcut - you can also use one of your limited\xa0
items to create new handholds on the fly. And'}, {'start': '92.880', 'end': '98.560', 'text': 'considering how this usually involves hurling\xa0
a piece of rusty rebar straight through thick,'}, {'start': '98.560', 'end': '103.840', 'text': 'industrial concrete, I wouldn’t be even\xa0
slightly surprised if it turns out that'}, {'start': '103.840', 'end': '110.160', 'text': 'the player character is actually just Popeye.\xa0
It would certainly explain how he replenishes'}, {'start': '110.160', 'end': '117.360', 'text': 'his supernatural strength by shotgunning cans of\xa0
what I can only assume is concentrated spinach.'}, {'start': '117.360', 'end': '123.280', 'text': "And that's pretty much it as far as the mechanics\xa0
are concerned. Yet despite how simple it all is,"}, {'start': '123.280', 'end': '129.280', 'text': 'there is a lot of depth, complexity and skill\xa0
expression to be found here. And more importantly,'}, {'start': '129.280', 'end': '135.200', 'text': "a lot of fun as well! Once you get into the right\xa0
rhythm there's just something mesmerizing about"}, {'start': '135.200', 'end': '141.760', 'text': 'swinging from handhold to handhold, making snap\xa0
decisions on when to expend stamina jumping and'}, {'start': '141.760', 'end': '147.280', 'text': 'when to take it slow, or just throwing\xa0
caution to the wind to take a supremely'}, {'start': '147.280', 'end': '153.200', 'text': "risky shortcut purely for the hell of it!
But it's when you get put under pressure"}, {'start': '153.200', 'end': '159.920', 'text': "that White Knuckle, or Sweaty Palm as it really\xa0
should've been called, becomes truly transcendent."}, {'start': '159.920', 'end': '165.200', 'text': "When there's danger all around you and you're\xa0
desperately trying to survive the onslaught just"}, {'start': '165.200', 'end': '172.400', 'text': "so you can get a tiny bit further than you've\xa0
ever been, that's when the magic happens. In"}, {'start': '172.400', 'end': '179.280', 'text': 'these moments I find that all rational thought\xa0
evaporates from my brain. I seem to enter a sort'}, {'start': '179.280', 'end': '184.560', 'text': 'of fugue state where the only things that exist\xa0
are the next few handholds and the obstacles'}, {'start': '184.560', 'end': '190.720', 'text': 'preventing me to reach them. Everything else\xa0
just kind of fades away until I reach a safe'}, {'start': '190.720', 'end': '201.360', 'text': 'space where I can finally relax, take a deep\xa0
breath and savor my victory - but only for a'}, {'start': '201.360', 'end': '208.560', 'text': "brief moment as there's always more to climb! 
It's not just the movement mechanics — the level"}, {'start': '208.560', 'end': '214.720', 'text': 'design is also rock solid despite being somewhat\xa0
procedurally generated on account of White Knuckle'}, {'start': '214.720', 'end': '220.080', 'text': 'being a roguelite. The way it works is that\xa0
each section you approach draws from a pool of'}, {'start': '220.080', 'end': '225.760', 'text': "hand-crafted 'levels' with a couple of elements\xa0
randomly added or removed in order to make them"}, {'start': '225.760', 'end': '232.000', 'text': "more replayable. Sometimes this means you'll have\xa0
to completely change your strategy as there's a"}, {'start': '232.000', 'end': '238.160', 'text': "nasty enemy in an unexpected place; sometimes\xa0
a pathway you're used to might become more"}, {'start': '238.160', 'end': '244.160', 'text': 'treacherous, and sometimes it might be as simple\xa0
as you getting a few extra items to incentivize'}, {'start': '244.160', 'end': '249.360', 'text': 'you to take the faster, riskier routes.
The downside of this approach is that'}, {'start': '249.360', 'end': '255.440', 'text': "you'll eventually see most of the variations,\xa0
especially in the first two zones as you'll be"}, {'start': '255.440', 'end': '262.000', 'text': 'frequently climbing through them to get back to\xa0
the much more difficult later stages of the game.'}, {'start': '262.000', 'end': '268.880', 'text': 'The upside is that all of the areas are actually\xa0
designed and tested by human beings which means'}, {'start': '268.880', 'end': '274.480', 'text': 'that all of them, and I really do mean all\xa0
of them, have a solid flow and work well with'}, {'start': '274.480', 'end': '280.240', 'text': "White Knuckle's mechanics. So as far as I'm\xa0
concerned, these light roguelite elements are"}, {'start': '280.240', 'end': '287.360', 'text': 'implemented really well - they add just enough\xa0
spice to keep each level fresh, but without'}, {'start': '287.360', 'end': '293.680', 'text': 'actually detracting from its quality.
And quality is exactly what they are, as'}, {'start': '293.680', 'end': '300.160', 'text': 'each individual chunk seems purpose-built around\xa0
celebrating a certain mechanic or obstacle type,'}, {'start': '300.160', 'end': '307.600', 'text': "which makes each one feel unique even though\xa0
they're all industrial nightmares. For example,"}, {'start': '307.600', 'end': '311.280', 'text': 'you can ask any White Knuckle player\xa0
what they think about the ventilator'}, {'start': '311.280', 'end': '315.920', 'text': "room with the button... and chances are\xa0
they'll instantly be able to draw a rough"}, {'start': '315.920', 'end': '323.120', 'text': 'layout from memory. The individual levels really\xa0
do stick out, and I think a big reason for that'}, {'start': '323.120', 'end': '329.840', 'text': "is that they're all at the center of at least one\xa0
story of glorious triumph or bitter failure."}, {'start': '329.840', 'end': '335.840', 'text': 'Another aspect of the level design that I greatly\xa0
appreciate is how clear and obvious the pathways'}, {'start': '335.840', 'end': '341.040', 'text': "are. Unless the room you're in is intentionally\xa0
cryptic to get you to make your own routes with"}, {'start': '341.040', 'end': '347.280', 'text': 'items or by using the environment, each area in\xa0
White Knuckle does a pretty good job of guiding'}, {'start': '347.280', 'end': '352.960', 'text': 'your view towards the next series of obstacles you\xa0
need to conquer - all the way to the very top.'}, {'start': '352.960', 'end': '357.600', 'text': "This might not sound like a big deal now,\xa0
but when you're frantically climbing away"}, {'start': '357.600', 'end': '363.920', 'text': 'from the grey sludge of doom devouring everything\xa0
below you, knowing where to go - and how to get'}, {'start': '363.920', 'end': '371.760', 'text': 'there quickly - becomes very important, very\xa0
fast. Oh and speaking of the sludge, that...'}, {'start': '371.760', 'end': '378.240', 'text': 'uhh, thing, essentially serves as a timer to\xa0
encourage you to push forward and utilize momentum'}, {'start': '378.240', 'end': '386.800', 'text': "to your advantage over simply playing it slow and\xa0
safe. It's terrifying when it's right behind you,"}, {'start': '386.800', 'end': '392.240', 'text': "and I've messed up plenty of times because\xa0
I panicked in its presence, but as far as"}, {'start': '392.240', 'end': '398.320', 'text': "world-ending eldritch horrors go it's actually\xa0
quite alright. You're never under *that* much"}, {'start': '398.320', 'end': '402.880', 'text': "pressure, so once you've gotten accustomed to\xa0
the movement mechanics you'll only ever have to"}, {'start': '402.880', 'end': '409.120', 'text': 'deal with it when you screw up *really* badly,\xa0
which is still preferable to simply getting'}, {'start': '409.120', 'end': '414.880', 'text': "annihilated and sent back to the start menu.
That said, you're still going to get quite"}, {'start': '414.880', 'end': '421.120', 'text': 'familiar with the start menu. While White Knuckle\xa0
is generally extremely fair with its challenges,'}, {'start': '421.120', 'end': '426.960', 'text': "it does not shy away from presenting you with\xa0
some truly devious gauntlets. I'd like to think"}, {'start': '426.960', 'end': '433.200', 'text': "I'm fairly experienced with its mechanics at this\xa0
point, and even still I find myself dying in the"}, {'start': '433.200', 'end': '440.960', 'text': "second or third zone because it's so easy to slip\xa0
up, panic instead of salvaging the situation,"}, {'start': '442.400', 'end': '447.200', 'text': 'and then dunk yourself directly\xa0
into the carnivorous sludge.'}, {'start': '447.200', 'end': '452.560', 'text': 'However, while it may be punishing to\xa0
the careless, White Knuckle is not cruel.'}, {'start': '452.560', 'end': '457.600', 'text': "The challenge ramps up relatively slowly, and\xa0
all of the crazy trials you'll have to best"}, {'start': '457.600', 'end': '464.560', 'text': 'later have very clear roots in the fairly easy\xa0
levels at the very start. So just by trying and'}, {'start': '464.560', 'end': '469.920', 'text': "failing you'll put in a decent amount of time\xa0
into practicing the basics. So while it might"}, {'start': '469.920', 'end': '476.640', 'text': 'seem annoying having to restart every time you\xa0
kick the bucket, the process of learning how'}, {'start': '476.640', 'end': '482.640', 'text': 'to speedrun those first few sections is exactly\xa0
what will make you better at tackling the wildest'}, {'start': '482.640', 'end': '487.520', 'text': "hazards White Knuckle can throw at you.
There's only one exception to all of this,"}, {'start': '487.520', 'end': '493.680', 'text': "and it's essentially my only real complaint with\xa0
White Knuckle. When you're climbing and you jump"}, {'start': '493.680', 'end': '501.120', 'text': "you'll expend a fair bit of stamina in order to\xa0
leap upwards as you would expect. But when you"}, {'start': '501.120', 'end': '506.320', 'text': "do that near an incline there's a chance you can\xa0
just launch yourself backwards which is almost"}, {'start': '506.320', 'end': '513.280', 'text': "guaranteed to be a run-ender. Whether this is\xa0
